analysis: The injury picture for Chicago widened materially on Tuesday: beyond LB T.J. Edwards (hamstring, DNP both days) and LB Jack Sanborn (concussion, DNP both days), starting RG Jonah Jackson (hip/quad, hurt in the Week 6 win over Atlanta) was limited Tuesday after sitting Monday and the Bears offensive coordinator was noncommittal on his Thursday availability, and RB Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) was limited Tuesday as well. New England offsets with only minor dings -- WR A.J. Brown (ankle) and CB Carlton Davis III (neck) both limited, neither trending toward missing. None of the four tracked books (BookMaker.eu, DraftKings, Caesars, FanDuel) have moved off Chicago -3/50.5 since Monday open, so the market has not yet priced any of this in.

The model now projects New England to win outright at 60.7% (up from 58.1% this morning) with Chicago covering just 29.6% of simulations and the total settling under the market number more often (66.3% under vs 33.7% over) as the injury-adjusted total gap widened to 44.6 vs the market 50.5. The no-vig moneyline gap is now real too: DK prices Chicago around 57% implied vs the model giving Chicago only about 39% win share. Two signal categories now agree (the model read and the expanded injury ledger), which is why both leans move up a notch; a market move (RLM/steam) would be a third confirming signal and has not shown up yet, so this is still the model and injuries leading the market rather than the market catching up.
